value: Why does syllabus v4.0.1 no longer use the phrase “completion criteria” for the binary “yes/no” exit criteria?
reason: The phrase no longer appears in 5.1.3 of v4.0.1; the card asked what it refers to there.

value: Version 4.0 used it for the yes/no kind alone, yet the glossary makes it a synonym of exit criteria; so v4.0.1 renamed that kind.
reason: The release note says the term was changed; the glossary lists completion criteria as a synonym of exit criteria.

value: The release notes list the change among the corrections, and 5.1.3 now says binary “yes/no” criteria, so “completion criteria” keeps its glossary sense of exit criteria.
reason: Explains why the rename matters, with both sources.

value: CTFL Syllabus v4.0.1, Appendix C “Release Notes”, “Corrections in the text”, p. 73; ISTQB Glossary, “exit criteria”
reason: The synonym fact comes from the glossary entry.

value: How far a test stands apart from the rest of the system: the more it depends on other parts, the less isolated it is.
reason: Glossing isolation as the degree of dependency contradicts the next cards, where higher layers depend more but have lower isolation.

value: The syllabus glosses isolation as the degree of dependency on other elements; read it as the inverse, since top-layer tests depend on most of the system and have the lowest isolation.
reason: Resolves the syllabus's reversed gloss for a newcomer.

value: Tests higher up rely on more of the rest of the system, so they are less isolated from it.
reason: The old explanation said isolation means dependency and falls going up, which implies higher tests depend less: the opposite of the model.
